html:
The handover of the Bakassi peninsula, a swampy, oil-rich strip on the border with Nigeria, to Cameroon, after the International Court of Justice ruled in Cameroon's favour on 10 October 2002.

The two countries had fought over it in 1981 and in the 1990s. The court based its ruling on a 1913 treaty between Britain and Germany. Most of the inhabitants were Nigerian fishing people. Nigeria, under President Obasanjo, accepted the ruling in the Greentree Agreement of 2006 and completed the handover on 14 August 2008. Some residents moved to Nigeria. See also German Kamerun and Nigeria.
